title: Mechanosynthesis of High Entropy Ceramics of MgAlTiCrNi System
content: In the last decade, high-entropy ceramics (HECeramics) have attracted much attention, especially high-entropy carbides and high-entropy borides (HECs and HEBs) [1]. HECs and HEBs consist of networks of disordered metal cations in combination with sublattices of carbon and boron anions [2]. The structural arrangement of HECeramics can combine excellent thermo-mechanical properties and thermodynamic stability generated by high entropy stability in the structure [3]. These materials have recently demonstrated excellent mechanical, electrical, thermal, magnetic and electrochemical properties [4]. A further advantage of HECeramics is its mechanical properties, which are resistant to extreme temperature and pressure conditions. Thus, they can be used as thermal protection coatings for aerospace applications, cutting tools, wear and drilling [5]. However, the atomic bonds of carbon or boron with metals often require a high temperature and a high pressure for their formation [6]. Therefore, methods such as hot pressing, electric arc plasma melting, spark plasma, and chemical vapor deposition have been used to fabricate HECeramics [7]. These synthesis processes for the fabrication of HECeramics are inefficient and challenging to control and replicate the operating conditions [8]. Therefore, using a synthesis method of HECeramics before sintering is crucial. It is precisely high-energy mechanical milling that fulfills these characteristics, where the diffusion of carbon in the structure is induced mechanically, so it has potential as a synthesis method [9]. However, few studies have reported HECeramics forming with low-density elements such as Mg and Al. Therefore, in this study, we report the synthesis and characterization of high entropy carbides and borides of MgAlTiCrNi High Entropy Alloys (HEA) obtained by high-energy mechanical milling.
